papers.title: Symptom Terminology Normalization in Traditional Chinese Medicine: Development and Evaluation of a 2-Stage Deep Learning Framework Based on Fine-Grained Semantic Classification.
papers.abstract: Due to the heterogeneity of symptom terminology and the lack of industry standards, the same symptom is often described using multiple expressions. Current normalization approaches struggle to comprehensively retrieve standard terms when a raw term maps to multiple symptoms.
papers.summary: This paper develops a two-stage deep learning framework for normalizing symptom terminology in Traditional Chinese Medicine, addressing the problem that the same symptom is often expressed in many different ways and that a single raw term can map to multiple standard symptoms. The approach uses fine-grained semantic classification to improve retrieval of correct standard terms, and the authors evaluate its performance against existing normalization methods.

papers.title: Predicting disease flares in axial spondyloarthritis using different machine learning models in the METEOR-SpA registry.
papers.abstract: To develop and externally validate machine learning models for predicting disease flares in axial spondyloarthritis (axSpA) using real-world registry data.
papers.summary: This study develops and externally validates machine learning models to predict disease flares in axial spondyloarthritis using real-world registry data from the METEOR-SpA cohort. The work demonstrates the feasibility of applying ML to registry data for flare prediction, which could support proactive clinical management. External validation strengthens confidence in the models' generalizability.

papers.title: Multimodality detection of early relapse in radically treated high-risk HPV-negative head and neck squamous cell carcinoma: study protocol for a prospective multicentre UK cohort study (HERD).
papers.abstract: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) is the seventh most common cancer globally, with over 12 000 new cases annually in the UK. Despite aggressive radical treatment, approximately 50% of patients with locally advanced (stage III/IV), human papilloma virus (HPV)-negative disease relapse within 2 years, often in the first year. Although current post-treatment follow-up schedules are recommended by clinical guidelines, imaging surveillance is led by symptoms after the initial 3 months and reliable biomarkers for early relapse are lacking. Consequently, recurrences are frequently detected
papers.summary: This paper presents the protocol for HERD, a prospective multicentre UK cohort study designed to detect early relapse in patients with radically treated, high-risk HPV-negative head and neck squamous cell carcinoma. The study aims to combine multiple modalities—likely imaging, blood-based biomarkers, and clinical data—to identify recurrences earlier than current symptom-driven surveillance allows, addressing a major unmet need in a patient group with ~50% relapse within two years.

papers.title: Learning Protein-Protein Binding Free Energies from Interface Graphs and Physicochemical Descriptors.
papers.abstract: Predicting protein-protein binding free energy (ΔG) from structure remains a central challenge in computational biophysics. Here, we present GULP (Graph-based Unified Learning for Protein binding), a graph neural network (GNN) that jointly learns from a residue-level graph representation of the binding interface and global physicochemical descriptors. We systematically investigate how training data distribution affects model performance by comparing a full training set with a balanced subset enriched for extreme-affinity complexes. GULP is computationally efficient and provides interpretable i
papers.summary: GULP is a graph neural network that predicts protein-protein binding free energy by combining residue-level interface graphs with global physicochemical descriptors. The authors show that training data distribution, particularly enrichment for extreme-affinity complexes, affects model performance, and the model is computationally efficient and interpretable.

papers.title: Integrated Systems Toxicology Analysis and Molecular Dynamics Study Reveal the Potential Mechanism by which Benzo[a]pyrene Contributes to Depression in Lung Adenocarcinoma via RNASE1 Upregulation.
papers.abstract: Benzo-[a]-pyrene (Bap), a prominent carcinogen found in tobacco smoke and air pollution, is closely associated with lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) and subsequent depression, though the mechanism underlying this comorbidity remains unclear. LUAD patients were categorized based on depression-related gene expression. Prognostic genes identified through machine learning were cross-referenced with predicted Bap targets. Mendelian randomization (MR) evaluated the causal relationship between RNASE1 and depression. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), molecular docking, and 100 ns molecular dynamics (M
papers.summary: This study integrates systems toxicology, machine learning, Mendelian randomization, single-cell RNA sequencing, and molecular dynamics to uncover how benzo[a]pyrene exposure may drive depression in lung adenocarcinoma patients through upregulation of RNASE1. The findings suggest RNASE1 as a potential mechanistic link and therapeutic target connecting smoking-related carcinogen exposure, LUAD, and comorbid depression.

papers.title: Chemically Informed Machine Learning Approach for Prediction of Reactivity Ratios in Radical Copolymerization.
papers.abstract: Predicting monomer reactivity ratios is crucial for controlling monomer sequence distribution in copolymers and their properties. Traditional experimental methods of determining reactivity ratios are time-consuming and resource-intensive, while existing computational methods often struggle with accuracy or scalability. Here, we present a method that combines unsupervised learning with artificial neural networks to predict reactivity ratios in radical copolymerization. By applying spectral clustering to physicochemical features of monomers, we identified three distinct monomer groups with chara
papers.summary: This paper introduces a machine learning approach that combines spectral clustering of monomer physicochemical features with artificial neural networks to predict reactivity ratios in radical copolymerization. The method aims to overcome the time and resource demands of experimental determination and the accuracy/scalability limits of prior computational approaches. It identifies three distinct monomer groups to inform predictions.

papers.title: BiMSGP: A Bidirectional Mamba-Based Model for Scalable and Accurate Genomic Prediction in Plants.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Accurate prediction of complex traits from high-dimensional genomic markers remains difficult in plant breeding. Linear models have limited capacity for non-linear interactions, and many deep learning models scale poorly on long marker sequences. This study introduces BiMSGP, a bidirectional Mamba-based model for scalable genomic prediction. Methods: BiMSGP extends a selective state space model with forward and backward processing so that each marker can integrate sequence context from both directions while retaining linear computational complexity; this is a modeling de
papers.summary: BiMSGP is a bidirectional Mamba-based deep learning model for genomic prediction in plant breeding that processes marker sequences in both forward and backward directions while maintaining linear computational complexity. It aims to capture non-linear interactions among high-dimensional genomic markers more scalably than existing deep learning approaches. The work targets improved accuracy and scalability for predicting complex traits from genomic data.

papers.title: CDELDA: A Content-Based Dual-Encoder for Cold-Start lncRNA-Disease Association Prediction.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: An important challenge in long non-coding RNA (lncRNA)-disease association prediction is prioritizing candidates when neither target node has association records in the training data, even though content features are available. This study aimed to develop and evaluate a content-based model for this both-cold setting. Methods: We developed CDELDA, a dual-encoder model combining lncRNA sequence, structure, and expression features with disease text, semantic similarity, and ontology-structure features. CDELDA was compared with five baseline methods on a normalized benchmark
papers.summary: CDELDA is a dual-encoder machine learning model that predicts associations between long non-coding RNAs and diseases even when neither the lncRNA nor the disease has any prior known associations in the training data (the 'both-cold' scenario). It combines lncRNA sequence, structure, and expression features with disease text, semantic similarity, and ontology features, and was benchmarked against five baseline methods.

papers.title: Bridging Nano-Interface Interactions and Organ-Specific Toxicity: A Review of Machine Learning for Nanomaterials Risk Assessment.
papers.abstract: Risk assessment of engineered nanomaterials (ENMs) is essential for protecting human health and the environment. Traditional hazard assessments rely primarily on in vivo testing, which faces technical challenges in extrapolation validity, ethical dilemmas, and high costs. Machine learning (ML) models offer alternative approaches that are aligned with the 3R principles (Replacement, Reduction, and Refinement) for reducing animal use. ML methods help address the economic, ethical, and temporal limitations of traditional nanotoxicology while advancing mechanistic understanding. This review presen
papers.summary: This review examines how machine learning models can predict the toxicity of engineered nanomaterials, offering an alternative to traditional in vivo animal testing. It highlights how ML approaches support the 3R principles (Replacement, Reduction, Refinement) while improving mechanistic understanding of nano-interface interactions and organ-specific toxicity. The paper surveys current methods and challenges in applying ML to nanomaterial risk assessment.

papers.title: Retrieval-Guided Transfer Learning for Low-Resource Ebola Drug-Target Affinity Prediction.
papers.abstract: Drug-target affinity (DTA) prediction plays an important role in computational drug discovery; however, its application to emerging infectious diseases such as Ebola remains challenging because of the limited availability of experimentally measured affinity data. To address this low-resource setting, we propose a retrieval-guided transfer-learning framework that leverages BindingDB interactions to improve Ebola DTA prediction. The framework uses a two-stage strategy. In Stage I, source interactions are selected using random sampling, compound-similarity retrieval, protein-similarity retrieval,
papers.summary: This paper presents a retrieval-guided transfer-learning framework for predicting drug-target binding affinity in Ebola, where experimental data are scarce. It leverages the large BindingDB interaction dataset, using compound- and protein-similarity retrieval to select relevant source data for transfer to the low-resource Ebola target. The approach aims to improve DTA prediction accuracy for emerging infectious diseases with limited training data.

papers.title: Multi-Omics and Machine Learning Identify Immune-Linked Gene Signatures for LUAD Stratification.
papers.abstract: Background: Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) is the most common subtype of non-small-cell lung cancer and is one of the leading causes of cancer-related deaths globally. Despite current developments, reliable biomarkers for effective diagnosis, prognosis, and patient stratification are still lacking. Methods: We analyzed publicly available TCGA-LUAD and GEO datasets using integrative bioinformatics approaches, including differential gene expression, weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), survival modeling, mutation profiling, immune cell infiltration scores, machine learning, and bulk
papers.summary: This study integrates transcriptomic and clinical data from TCGA-LUAD and GEO to identify immune-linked gene signatures that can stratify lung adenocarcinoma patients by prognosis. Using WGCNA, survival modeling, mutation profiling, immune infiltration analysis, and machine learning, the authors derive gene signatures associated with immune status and patient outcomes. The work highlights candidate biomarkers for improved diagnosis and risk stratification in LUAD.

papers.title: Innovative Applications of Artificial Intelligence in Bacteriophage Research: A New Chapter in Future Medicine.
papers.abstract: As the crisis of antibiotic resistance escalates, phage therapy has regained attention as an alternative strategy. Artificial intelligence (AI) technologies offer new avenues to overcome the bottlenecks inherent in traditional bacteriophage research. This review summarizes the multi-dimensional innovative applications of machine learning, deep learning, and large biological models in phage studies. In the fields of phage recognition and genomics, support vector machines (SVMs), convolutional neural networks (CNNs), and pre-trained protein language models can all achieve recognition accuracy ra
papers.summary: This review surveys how machine learning, deep learning, and large biological models are being applied across bacteriophage research, including phage recognition, genomics, and protein language modeling. It argues that AI can help overcome bottlenecks in traditional phage research as interest in phage therapy grows amid antibiotic resistance. The abstract is truncated, but the scope covers multiple AI methods achieving high recognition accuracy for phage-related tasks.

papers.title: Routine Laboratory-Based Machine Learning for Discriminating Multiple Myeloma from Clinical Mimickers: Development and Internal Validation of a Diagnostic Prediction Model.
papers.abstract: Background: Multiple myeloma (MM) diagnosis requires specialised testing that is not universally available, contributing to diagnostic delays. The aim of this study was to develop and internally validate statistical and machine learning (ML) models that discriminate MM from clinically similar conditions using exclusively routine laboratory parameters. Methods: This retrospective diagnostic prediction model study included 422 consecutive patients referred to hematology for suspected MM at a tertiary care center (2017-2025). Fifteen routine demographic and laboratory variables were used to train
papers.summary: This study developed and internally validated machine learning models that distinguish multiple myeloma from clinically similar conditions using only routine laboratory and demographic data from 422 patients. The approach aims to enable earlier diagnosis in settings where specialized testing is unavailable, potentially reducing diagnostic delays.

papers.title: Development of an Interpretable QSAR Model for Predicting Coagulation Factor XIIa Inhibitors Using Ensemble Machine Learning.
papers.abstract: Background/Objective: Activated coagulation factor XII (FXIIa) is a component of the contact activation pathway and a pharmacologically relevant target in contact-system-associated processes. In this study, scaffold-aware and interpretable machine-learning QSAR models were developed for human FXIIa activity. Methods: Bioactivity records for the human single protein target CHEMBL2821 were retrieved from ChEMBL release 37. Modeling was restricted to exact IC50 measurements from assays explicitly referring to FXIIa, Factor XIIa, or activated Factor XII. Median-consolidated pIC50 values and two-di
papers.summary: This study developed interpretable machine-learning QSAR models to predict the inhibitory activity of compounds against coagulation factor XIIa (FXIIa), a target in the contact activation pathway. Using IC50 data from ChEMBL, the authors built ensemble models with scaffold-aware validation and interpretability features to identify key structural determinants of FXIIa inhibition. The work provides a predictive tool for early-stage drug discovery targeting contact-system-related processes.

papers.title: Biopesticidal Potential of the Cannabis sativa L. Metabolites: A Denoised, Docking-Informed QSAR Model.
papers.abstract: Plant metabolites are a promising source of new biopesticides, but their chemical diversity exceeds the capacity of experimental screening. Cannabis sativa is a particularly attractive crop for discovering such compounds, although its metabolome has not been systematically evaluated for biopesticidal potential. Here, we computationally analyzed 5211 compounds annotated as C. sativa metabolites in the Cannabis Compound Database (CCD) using an integrated framework combining graph-based molecular prediction and protein-ligand interaction analysis. Initial prioritization employed a directed messag
papers.summary: This study computationally screened 5,211 Cannabis sativa metabolites for biopesticidal potential using a docking-informed QSAR model combined with graph-based molecular prediction. The integrated framework prioritized candidate compounds by predicting bioactivity and protein-ligand interactions, offering a scalable way to mine plant metabolomes for new pesticides. It demonstrates a proof-of-concept pipeline for computational biopesticide discovery from underexplored plant chemical diversity.

papers.title: Computational and AI-Enabled Imaging Biomarkers for Predicting and Assessing Immunotherapy Response in Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma: A Systematic Review with Functional Meta-Synthesis.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Computational and artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled imaging biomarkers are increasingly being investigated for immunotherapy-response assessment in oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC), but the evidence is heterogeneous. This systematic review identified, critically appraised, and synthesized imaging biomarkers used to predict or assess observed immunotherapy response in OSCC. Methods: PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and Scopus were searched from inception to 31 July 2026, without language restrictions. The protocol was registered in PROSPERO. Eligible studies evaluated quanti
papers.summary: This systematic review synthesizes evidence on computational and AI-based imaging biomarkers for predicting or assessing immunotherapy response in oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC). The authors critically appraise the heterogeneous literature and provide a functional meta-synthesis of the imaging biomarkers investigated to date. The work highlights the current state and limitations of AI-enabled imaging approaches in this clinical context.

papers.title: Deep Learning-Guided Identification and In Vivo Validation of Compact Cis-Regulatory Elements for the Zebrafish Habenula.
papers.abstract: Precise genetic access to the zebrafish habenula remains limited by a scarcity of compact, sequence-defined cis-regulatory elements (CREs). Here, we integrated developmental expression mapping, deep-learning predictions on long-range sequences, and in vivo reporter assays to identify compact regulatory sequences driving habenular expression.
papers.summary: This study combines developmental expression mapping with deep-learning predictions on long-range genomic sequences to identify compact cis-regulatory elements (CREs) that drive gene expression specifically in the zebrafish habenula. The predicted CREs were validated in vivo using reporter assays, providing new sequence-defined tools for precise genetic targeting of this brain region.

papers.title: From Machine Learning-Enhanced Proteomics to a Validated Diagnostic Model: A Pipeline for Breast Cancer Biomarker Discovery via Independent and Transcriptomic Corroboration.
papers.abstract: Early diagnosis of breast cancer (BC) remains challenging. The limited sensitivity and specificity of existing serum tumor markers for reliable clinical application highlight the need to develop a more accurate and efficient screening workflow. This study analyzed serum samples from 255 breast cancer patients and 300 healthy controls using matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization time-of-flight (MALDI-TOF) mass spectrometry, identifying 58 differentially expressed peptides (37 upregulated, 21 downregulated). Combined with machine learning, peptide identification, and external validation, a
papers.summary: This study used MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry to profile serum peptides from 255 breast cancer patients and 300 healthy controls, identifying 58 differentially expressed peptides. By combining machine learning with peptide identification and external validation, the authors developed and validated a diagnostic model for breast cancer, with additional corroboration from transcriptomic data.

papers.title: A Robust Masked Painter Framework for Gene Selection in Binary Classification of High-Dimensional Functional Genomic Data.
papers.abstract: High-dimensional gene expression datasets in chemometric and biomedical research present significant challenges for machine learning because the number of genes greatly exceeds the number of available samples, increasing the risk of overfitting and reducing classification reliability. Existing gene selection methods are often sensitive to noise and outliers, leading to unstable feature subsets and degraded classification performance. To address these limitations, this study proposes a Robust Masked Painter (RMP) framework that integrates robust measures of location and dispersion, namely the M
papers.summary: This paper introduces the Robust Masked Painter (RMP) framework, a gene selection method designed to handle high-dimensional functional genomic data where genes vastly outnumber samples. By incorporating robust statistical measures of location and dispersion, RMP aims to reduce sensitivity to noise and outliers, yielding more stable feature subsets and improved binary classification performance.

papers.title: A Systematic Machine Learning Framework for Evaluating and Ranking Omics Layers in Cancer Drug Response Prediction.
papers.abstract: This study introduces a top-down framework for evaluating the utility of multi-omics features to predict the response of 309 drugs in cancer cell lines. This was done by taking a multi-omics approach where data from proteomic, transcriptomic, genomic, metabolomic, and miRNA were integrated with drug sensitivity (area under the curve, AUC) data. We performed modular dimensionality reduction using t-SNE (t-distributed Stochastic Neighbor Embedding), followed by K-Means clustering to stratify cell lines into data-driven molecular subgroups, and applied a Random Forest model to refine the drug lis
papers.summary: This study builds a machine learning framework to test how well different omics layers (proteomics, transcriptomics, genomics, metabolomics, miRNA) predict cancer drug response across 309 drugs in cell lines. Using t-SNE dimensionality reduction, K-Means clustering, and Random Forest models, the authors rank which omics data types are most informative for drug sensitivity prediction. The work provides a systematic comparison of omics layer utility in pharmacogenomic modeling.

papers.title: Cross-Model Uncertainty-Aware Minimal Editing of Cis-Regulatory Elements for Cell-Type-Selective Design.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Cis-regulatory elements (CREs) help mediate cell-type-selective gene expression, yet sequence-to-activity models are rarely converted into compact, experimentally tractable variant panels that retain natural regulatory scaffolds. We developed SafeEdit-CRE to select minimal edits that preserve cross-model specificity while reducing predictive uncertainty, yielding an auditable CRE variant library for reporter-screening prioritization. Methods: SafeEdit-CRE combines the published Malinois sequence-activity predictor with an architecture-distinct reviewer ensemble, validati
papers.summary: SafeEdit-CRE is a computational framework that designs minimal edits to cis-regulatory elements (CREs) to achieve cell-type-selective gene expression while preserving natural regulatory scaffolds. It combines the Malinois sequence-to-activity predictor with an architecture-distinct reviewer ensemble to reduce predictive uncertainty and produce an auditable variant library for reporter-screening prioritization.

papers.title: Resnet-Driven In Silico Identification of Lead Peptides from the Venom Gland Transcriptome of Orientothele washanensis Coupled with Molecular Docking and Dynamics Simulation.
papers.abstract: Background: Orientothele washanensis is a venomous spider with considerable ecological and scientific importance. Its venom, characterized by complex composition and ease of collection, serves as a valuable resource for the discovery of natural peptide drugs. Conventional wet-lab screening methods are limited by rigorous experimental conditions, high resource consumption, and long research cycles, which hinder the efficient identification of functional peptides from the venom gland transcriptome of this spider. Methods: To address these technical bottlenecks, this study developed a novel deep
papers.summary: This study uses a ResNet-based deep learning approach to identify potential peptide drug leads from the venom gland transcriptome of the spider Orientothele washanensis, bypassing traditional wet-lab screening. Candidate peptides were then validated in silico using molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations to assess binding stability and interactions.

papers.title: Identification and Preliminary mRNA Validation of Key Genes Associated with Tolerogenic Dendritic Cells in Keloid Based on Transcriptome Data.
papers.abstract: Keloid is a cutaneous fibrotic disorder characterized by excessive fibrous tissue proliferation during wound healing. Tolerogenic dendritic cells (tolDCs) may participate in keloid immunopathology, but the related molecular signatures remain unclear. This study aimed to identify candidate tolDC-associated genes in keloid by integrating tolDC-related transcriptomic profiles with keloid transcriptomic datasets.
papers.summary: This study integrates tolerogenic dendritic cell (tolDC) transcriptomic profiles with keloid transcriptome datasets to identify candidate genes linking tolDCs to keloid pathology. The authors identify key tolDC-associated genes and perform preliminary mRNA validation, suggesting a potential immune-mediated mechanism in keloid formation. The findings highlight tolDC-related molecular signatures as possible targets for further keloid research.

papers.title: Integrative Transcriptomic and Genetic Analyses Identify CDC20 as a Potential Biomarker Associated with Cell Cycle and Immune-Inflammatory Processes in Psoriasis.
papers.abstract: To identify psoriasis-associated candidate genes and regulatory features via integrated transcriptomic, immune and genetic analyses, and validate them in an imiquimod-induced psoriasis-like murine model.
papers.summary: This study integrates transcriptomic, immune, and genetic analyses to identify CDC20 as a candidate biomarker for psoriasis, linking it to cell cycle regulation and immune-inflammatory processes. The findings were validated in an imiquimod-induced psoriasis-like mouse model, supporting CDC20's potential relevance to disease mechanisms.

papers.title: AI-driven genotype-phenotype modeling: a framework integrating multi-modal single-cell genomics and reverse vaccinology for de novo design of multi-epitope cancer vaccines.
papers.abstract: Cancer vaccines have emerged as a promising strategy for personalized cancer immunotherapy; however, their development has traditionally relied on bulk sequencing approaches that average molecular information across millions of cells, thereby obscuring the extensive intratumoral heterogeneity that drives disease progression, therapeutic resistance, and immune escape. Recent advances in multi-modal single-cell genomics have transformed the ability to characterize tumors at unprecedented resolution, enabling the identification of distinct cellular populations, clonal evolutionary trajectories, a
papers.summary: This paper proposes a computational framework that combines multi-modal single-cell genomics with reverse vaccinology to model genotype-phenotype relationships and design multi-epitope cancer vaccines de novo. It argues that single-cell resolution can capture intratumoral heterogeneity that bulk sequencing misses, potentially improving the identification of vaccine targets. The abstract is truncated, so the concrete results and validation remain unclear.

papers.title: Integrative computational analysis of public fecal lipidomics and transcriptomics datasets suggests a candidate association between the COX-2 pathway and CE(20:4) in colorectal adenoma-carcinoma progression.
papers.abstract: The fecal lipidomic changes underlying the colorectal adenoma-carcinoma sequence remain incompletely characterized, particularly regarding the continuous metabolic trajectory and heterogeneity of precancerous adenomas. We aimed to use publicly available multi-omics data and an integrative computational framework to identify candidate lipidomic features associated with a CRC-like metabolic state in adenomas.
papers.summary: This study integrates public fecal lipidomics and transcriptomics datasets to identify lipidomic features associated with a colorectal cancer-like metabolic state in precancerous adenomas. The analysis suggests a candidate link between the COX-2 pathway and the lipid species CE(20:4) along the adenoma-carcinoma progression sequence. The findings are computational and hypothesis-generating, requiring experimental validation.

papers.title: A hybrid ICA-GRU approach for forecasting gold futures price.
papers.abstract: Accurate forecasting of gold futures prices is very important for investors and analysts due to the highly volatile and nonlinear nature of the commodity markets. This research work develops a hybrid ICA-GRU framework to gold futures price forecasting by developing a hybrid approach of ICA and GRU-based neural networks. The historical daily gold futures price data spanning from 2015 to 2026 were collected from Yahoo Finance. ICA transforms correlated financial variables into statistically independent components, generating informative latent feature representations that may better capture the
papers.summary: This paper proposes a hybrid model combining Independent Component Analysis (ICA) with a Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) neural network to forecast gold futures prices. Using daily gold futures data from 2015 to 2026, ICA extracts statistically independent latent features from correlated financial variables, which are then fed into the GRU for prediction. The approach aims to improve accuracy in the highly volatile and nonlinear commodity market.

papers.title: External validation of the CALLY index and development of a laboratory-based model for 28-day mortality in sepsis: a two-center study.
papers.abstract: Early identification of high-risk sepsis patients remains challenging. The C-reactive protein-Albumin-Lymphocyte (CALLY) index, which integrates inflammation, nutritional status, and immune function, may hold prognostic value in this setting.
papers.summary: This two-center study externally validates the CALLY index (combining CRP, albumin, and lymphocyte count) as a prognostic marker for 28-day mortality in sepsis patients and develops a laboratory-based predictive model. The work suggests that a simple, routinely available blood test composite could help clinicians identify high-risk sepsis patients early.

papers.title: Structured environmental cues and youth sports consumption: an AI-powered behavioral modeling approach.
papers.abstract: Physical inactivity among children and adolescents represents a critical global public health challenge, imposing an annual economic burden exceeding $27 billion on healthcare systems worldwide. Despite this pressing concern, the complex, cross-level relationships between structured environmental cues-spanning household, school, and community domains-and youth sports consumption remain inadequately understood, particularly across the heterogeneous urbanrural continuum characteristic of rapidly developing economies.
papers.summary: This study uses AI-powered behavioral modeling to examine how structured environmental cues across household, school, and community domains relate to youth sports consumption, with attention to urban-rural differences in developing economies. The work aims to clarify cross-level influences on physical inactivity among children and adolescents, a major public health concern.

papers.title: Proteomic machine-learning signatures associated with carotid plaque: A population-based hypothesis-generating study.
papers.abstract: Carotid plaque (CP) is a surrogate marker of cardiovascular disease, and high-risk morphology significantly increases the risk of stroke. The aim of this study was to develop advanced machine learning (ML) models to predict the presence of CP in the general population. The study involved 693 participants from the Polish Longitudinal University Study - Bialystok PLUS, a representative sample of the local population. The analysis used 460 OLINK protein biomarkers. The data were analysed using the BORUTA algorithm based on the random forest classifier method. We identified 42 significant biomarke
papers.summary: This population-based study used machine learning (BORUTA/random forest) on 460 OLINK protein biomarkers from 693 participants to identify proteomic signatures associated with carotid plaque presence. The authors identified 42 significant biomarkers, suggesting that proteomic ML models could help predict carotid plaque in the general population. As a hypothesis-generating study, it lays groundwork for larger validation efforts.
